{"self_assessment": "Impact: We built a fish with a rounded body, a pointed nose, and a forked tail, and by my read of the table all 113 standing dominoes were connected to the start before the push. I haven't seen the judge's verdict, so I can't claim it was recognized. Two things could have helped it: we never added an eye, and the tail came out a bit odd. We also finished with 137 dominoes unused, so there was room to add detail. I chose safety over polish at the end.

Execution: I laid the start and the top line, which fell cleanly from the start. After that I mostly did checks and small fixes, like nudging a kink and one misaligned domino at the lower tip. I left a harmless stray domino on the bottom line rather than risk a bump. I should have run a proper inspect on the tail joints instead of only looking. Some time was lost to confusion over stroke numbers when the tail was added to the pad, and I could have caught that sooner.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed and tried to stay out of people's way while Leo laid the back edge and Maya and Tom finished the bottom line. I asked Tom about the stray piece and thanked people for their work. I did talk over the pad handoff a bit early, since Maya wanted it, and I said the sketch was done when the tail wasn't actually on it. That added to the mix-up.

Leadership: I helped settle on the fish quickly, split the strokes, and kept things calm and upbeat as time ran down. Leo and Maya also steered a lot, so I wasn't the only one. If I did it again, I'd use the spare time and dominoes to add an eye and check the tail outline against the sketch, instead of declaring us done early."}
